name: Wrist prep routine

technique.setup: Start with wrist circles standing, then kneel on all fours with hands under the shoulders. Do each drill for 8-10 slow reps: rocks forward and back with fingers forward, fingers to the sides, fingers back, then palm lifts and finger pulses.
cues: Fingers spread and gripping the floor
Move slowly and only into easy range
Shift weight gradually, knees take most of it
Breathe and keep the shoulders relaxed
mistakes: Rushing through it or skipping it before hand-balancing
Forcing the end range with full bodyweight
Collapsing into the heel of the hand
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist
Numbness or tingling in the fingers

media.searchHint: GMB Fitness wrist warm up routine for handstands

notes: The warm-up for every hand-balancing and straight-arm exercise. About 3-5 minutes; do it every session before handstand, HSPU or planche work. With a sore wrist, do only the circles and gentle unloaded stretches.

name: Wall plank

technique.setup: Sit with your back to the wall and mark where your feet reach. Put your hands on that spot, then walk the feet up the wall to hip height so the body forms an L.
cues: Fingers spread and gripping, push the floor away
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
Stack shoulders over the wrists
Look between your hands
mistakes: Hands too far from the wall so the shoulders sit behind the wrists
Sagging into the shoulders instead of pushing tall
Arching the lower back
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder
Dizziness or a pounding head

media.searchHint: GMB Fitness L handstand wall plank tutorial

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Walk the feet down to come out.

name: Wall walk

technique.setup: Start in a push-up position with the feet against the wall. Walk the feet up the wall while walking the hands in, stopping about a hand's length from the wall, then walk back down the same way.
cues: Fingers spread and gripping, push the floor away
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
Small steps with hands and feet
Look between your hands
mistakes: Walking the hands so close the body tips into the wall
Rushing the walk down and collapsing
Banana back with ribs flared
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder
Dizziness or a pounding head

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Only walk as close to the wall as you can control on the way down.

name: Chest-to-wall handstand hold

technique.setup: Walk up the wall as in the wall walk until the hands are a hand's length from it and the chest faces the wall, body close to vertical. Come down by walking the hands out and the feet down.
cues: Fingers spread and gripping, push the floor away
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
Legs together, toes pointed
Look between your hands
mistakes: Banana back with ribs flared
Shrugging down into the shoulders
Hands too far from the wall
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder
Dizziness or a pounding head

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs chest to wall handstand tutorial

notes: Do wrist-prep first. A 60 s hold is the gate for freestanding handstand drills.

name: Wall handstand shoulder taps

technique.setup: Get into a chest-to-wall handstand. Shift your weight onto one hand, lift the other and tap that shoulder, then place it back and switch sides.
cues: Fingers spread and gripping, push the floor away
Shift weight slowly before lifting the hand
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
Look between your hands
mistakes: Snatching the hand off without shifting weight first
Hips swinging side to side
Sinking into the standing shoulder
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder
Dizziness or a pounding head

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs chest to wall handstand shoulder taps

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Start with a light fingertip lift before full taps.

name: Handstand kick-up (back to wall)

technique.setup: Practise the cartwheel bail first: from a lunge, place the hands, and if you tip over, turn one hand out and step down to the side. Then place the hands a hand's length from the wall, kick up with a straight leg so the heels softly touch the wall, hold a few seconds and step down.
cues: Fingers spread and gripping, push the floor away
Kick with a straight leg, just enough to reach the wall
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
Look between your hands
mistakes: Kicking too hard and slamming the heels into the wall
Bending the arms on the kick
Throwing the head back to look at the wall
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder
Dizziness or a pounding head

media.searchHint: GMB Fitness handstand kick up to wall and cartwheel bail

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Each rep is one kick-up with a 3-5 s hold. Clear space around you and practise the cartwheel bail before every session.

name: Freestanding handstand

technique.setup: Clear a space with soft flooring and nothing behind or beside you. Rehearse the cartwheel bail (turn one hand out and step down to the side) before kicking up with a controlled straight leg to find balance.
cues: Fingers spread, grip the floor to stop over-balancing
Push the floor away, shoulders by the ears
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
Look between your hands
mistakes: Falling flat on the back instead of cartwheeling out
Banana back with ribs flared
Bent arms or sinking shoulders
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist or shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder
Dizziness or a pounding head
Losing control of the bail or falling onto the back

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs freestanding handstand beginner tutorial bail out

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Gate: 60 s chest-to-wall hold. Many short attempts beat a few long ones; stop the session when attempts get sloppy.

name: Pike push-up

technique.setup: Start in a push-up position and walk the feet in until the hips are high in an upside-down V. Hands shoulder-width, fingers spread.
cues: Lower the head to a point in front of the hands
Elbows back at about 45 degrees, not flared
Keep the hips high over the shoulders
Push the floor away to finish
mistakes: Hips dropping so it turns into a push-up
Elbows flaring straight out
Half reps that stop well above the floor
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Journal dose was 6-10 x3-4.

name: Elevated pike push-up

technique.setup: Put the feet on a box and walk the hands back until the hips are stacked above the shoulders. Start low (knee height) and raise the box only when reps are clean.
cues: Lower the head to a point in front of the hands
Elbows back at about 45 degrees, not flared
Hips stacked over the shoulders
Push the floor away to finish
mistakes: Hands too far from the box so the hips drop
Elbows flaring straight out
Dropping fast onto the head
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pinching at the top of the shoulder
Neck pain or a pounding head

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs elevated pike push up progression

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Log the box height. 10 clean reps is the gate for wall HSPU work.

name: Wall handstand push-up negative

technique.setup: Put a folded cushion or ab mat under where your head will land, then kick or walk up into a wall handstand. Lower slowly over 3-5 seconds until the head gently touches the cushion, then come down off the wall and reset.
cues: Lower over 3-5 seconds, never drop
Head lands slightly in front of the hands, making a triangle
Elbows back, not flared
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
mistakes: Collapsing the last few centimetres onto the head
Elbows flaring straight out
Skipping the cushion
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Any neck pain or pressure
Dizziness or a pounding head

media.searchHint: FitnessFAQs wall handstand push up negative eccentric

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Gate: 10 elevated pike push-ups. Needs a cushion or ab mat under the head (not in the equipment list).

name: Wall handstand push-up

technique.setup: Put a folded cushion or ab mat under where your head will land and get into a wall handstand. Lower with control until the head lightly touches the cushion, then press back to straight arms.
cues: Lower with control, head in front of the hands
Elbows back, not flared
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
Push the floor away to lock out
mistakes: Dropping onto the head
Kicking off the wall to finish the rep
Banana back to cheat the press
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Any neck pain or pressure
Dizziness or a pounding head

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Gate: 10 elevated pike push-ups. Keep the cushion under the head.

name: Planche lean

technique.setup: Start in a push-up position with fingers turned slightly out. Lean the shoulders forward past the hands only as far as you can with straight arms.
cues: Arms locked straight
Push the floor away, round the upper back
Ribs in, squeeze glutes
Lean a little further each week, not each set
mistakes: Bending the elbows to lean further
Sagging hips or shoulders
Leaning too far too soon
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pain at the front of the elbow or in the biceps tendon

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Straight-arm work: at most one step per block. A 30 s lean plus 20 push-ups is the gate for planche work beyond leans.

name: Frog stand

technique.setup: Squat down, place the hands shoulder-width in front of the feet and rest the knees on the backs of the elbows. Put a cushion in front of you, then lean forward until the feet float.
cues: Fingers spread and gripping
Lean forward slowly until the feet lift
Push the floor away, upper back round
Look slightly ahead of the hands
mistakes: Leaning too far and tipping onto the face
Jumping the feet up instead of leaning
Letting the shoulders sink
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pain at the front of the elbow

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Gate: 20 push-ups, 30 s planche lean and wrist prep in place. Straight-arm work: at most one step per block.

name: Tuck planche

technique.setup: From a squat with hands beside the hips and arms straight, lean forward and lift the feet so the knees stay tucked to the chest and the hips rise to shoulder height.
cues: Arms locked straight
Push the floor away, round the upper back
Knees tight to the chest
Lean the shoulders forward past the hands
mistakes: Bending the elbows
Resting the knees on the arms (that is a frog stand)
Hips staying low
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pain at the front of the elbow or in the biceps tendon

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Gate: 20 push-ups, 30 s planche lean and wrist prep in place. Straight-arm work: at most one step per block; parallettes or dip bars ease the wrists if available.

name: Advanced tuck planche

technique.setup: From a tuck planche, open the hips so the back is flat and the knees move away from the chest, with the hips level with the shoulders.
cues: Arms locked straight
Push the floor away, back flat
Lean the shoulders forward past the hands
Squeeze glutes, knees tucked under the hips
mistakes: Bending the elbows
Rounding back into a regular tuck
Holding too long and losing the position
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pain at the front of the elbow or in the biceps tendon

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Gate: 20 push-ups, 30 s planche lean and wrist prep in place. Straight-arm work: at most one step per block; expect months at each step.

name: Straddle planche

technique.setup: From an advanced tuck planche, extend the legs straight and wide into a straddle, keeping the body level with the floor.
cues: Arms locked straight
Push the floor away, lean past the hands
Legs straight and wide, toes pointed
Squeeze glutes, ribs in
mistakes: Bending the elbows
Hips piking up above the shoulders
Rushing to this step before the advanced tuck is solid
stopIf: Sharp or joint pain in the wrist, elbow or shoulder
Pain at the front of the elbow or in the biceps tendon

notes: Do wrist-prep first. Gate: 20 push-ups, 30 s planche lean and wrist prep in place. Straight-arm work: at most one step per block; worth a coach session before starting.
